FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing has been executed and no results are claimed)

Title: Combined Jailbreak Techniques and ASR of LLMs under Token-Level (AutoDAN) and Prompt-Level (PAIR) Attacks — a Factorial Design

=====================================================================
(a) RATIONALE — TIE TO THE RESEARCH QUESTION
=====================================================================
The research question asks how COMBINED jailbreak techniques — attacker strength, defense strength, and previously tested tricks — affect ASR, and what the interaction dynamics between attacker power and defense robustness look like across datasets and attack styles. This demands a design in which these factors are varied ORTHOGONALLY rather than one at a time, because the primary scientific objects are interaction effects, not main effects. A crossed factorial (Attacker Strength × Defense Strength × Trick Combination) run separately under AutoDAN (token-level) and PAIR (prompt-level), stratified by dataset, directly yields: (i) whether stronger attacks overcome stronger defenses (attacker × defense interaction — e.g., an "arms-race" crossover where defense gains shrink as attacker strength grows); (ii) whether tricks and attacker strength substitute or complement (trick × attacker interaction); and (iii) whether these patterns generalize across datasets and across token-level vs. prompt-level attack styles (stratification). Prior-tested tricks enter as an explicit experimental factor rather than a fixed recipe, so their incremental and combined contribution is estimated rather than assumed. The workspace inspection confirmed this is a design-only track (task.json; track.md: "repositories and compute are not required"), so all concrete values below are DESIGN ASSUMPTIONS with stated fallbacks, not verified facts.

=====================================================================
(b) FULL VARIABLE SPECIFICATION AND FACTOR LEVELS
=====================================================================
Fixed requirements (given, not assumptions): AutoDAN = token-level attack; PAIR = prompt-level attack.

FACTOR 1 — ATTACKER STRENGTH (3 ordered levels; design assumption).
- Levels: Weak / Medium / Strong.
- AutoDAN operationalization (token-level): Weak = 1 GA run, small population, few generations (e.g., pop 20, 5 generations, 1 restart); Medium = pop 50, 20 generations, 2 restarts; Strong = pop 100, 50 generations, 4 restarts + best-of selection. (Values are placeholders consistent with the AutoDAN paper's search settings; fallback: adopt whatever the setup topics specify.)
- PAIR operationalization (prompt-level): Weak = depth N=3, breadth K=1, smaller attacker model; Medium = N=10, K=4; Strong = N=20, K=6, strongest available attacker model, temperature raised modestly for exploration.
- Cross-method comparability: "strength" is WITHIN-STYLE only; no numeric cross-style equivalence is claimed. Instead, both styles are matched on total target-model query budget per cell (see Controls), so strength is not confounded with raw search effort.

FACTOR 2 — DEFENSE STRENGTH (3-tier ladder; design assumption).
- L0 None (raw model) — baseline.
- L1 Weak: light input-side defenses — paraphrase-based input smoothing or system-prompt self-reminding.
- L2 Strong: robust defenses — SmoothLLM-style randomized smoothing with perturbation+vote, and/or output filtering; if infeasible, substitute a safety-hardened target variant as the "strong defense" arm (fallback noted).
- Rationale for a ladder rather than a binary: the attacker × defense interaction (diminishing defense returns vs. robust plateau) requires at least three points to characterize shape.

FACTOR 3 — TRICK COMBINATION (previously tested tricks; design assumption — exact inventory to be taken from setup topics if later supplied; otherwise the canonical PAIR/AutoDAN-tested set: persona/role-play, scenario nesting, refusal-suppression phrasing, obfuscation/encryption, few-shot exemplars).
- Levels: no-trick baseline; each single trick; all pairwise 2-trick combinations; one full 3-trick set (a deliberately "maximal" combination). Total 1 + 5 + 10 + 1 = 17 trick-set levels for a 5-trick inventory (scaled down if inventory differs).
- Trick order is permuted within combinations (see Controls).

FACTOR 4 (stratification) — ATTACK STYLE: AutoDAN vs. PAIR (fixed).
FACTOR 5 (stratification) — DATASET: AdvBench (stratified subsample of the 520 behaviors) + a second benchmark subset (e.g., HarmBench), giving two dataset strata.

TARGET MODELS (2–4; design assumption): Llama-2-7B-Chat (weaker safety alignment), Llama-3-8B-Instruct (stronger, newer), Mistral-7B-Instruct (different training lineage); optional 4th: a safety-hardened variant (serves as the strong-defense arm if L2 defenses are substituted). Scope limited to open-weight models: weights must be locally loadable for intervention-heavy defenses (SmoothLLM requires many perturbed queries). API-only targets would (i) multiply cost per query, (ii) break SmoothLLM-style smoothing feasibility at scale, and (iii) make fixed-seed reproducibility impossible; they would be restricted to a small PAIR-only supplementary cell if included at all.

JUDGE SPECIFICATION AND ASR DEFINITION (fixed within the design, with rationale):
- Primary judge: a strong LLM judge (e.g., Llama-3-70B-Instruct or GPT-4-class) with a rubric prompt asking for binary harmfulness given (behavior, response), plus the HarmBench classifier as a secondary judge.
- ASR definition: ASR(cell) = fraction of behaviors for which the judge returns "successful" (policy-violating, non-refusal, substantively on-target) for at least one response in the attack's best-of output. Threshold fixed a priori: judge probability ≥ 0.5 mapped to success, with sensitivity analysis at 0.3/0.7. Secondary metrics: ASR@budget (success within the matched query budget — the efficiency-normalized metric used for cross-strength comparison), mean queries-to-success among successes, and judge agreement (Cohen's κ) on the human-verified subsample.
- Rationale: a single fixed judge with sensitivity analysis avoids threshold-shopping; dual-judging plus a ~10% human-verified subsample bounds judge bias, which is the main threat to interaction estimates.

=====================================================================
(c) CONTROLS
=====================================================================
1. Baselines: (i) no-attack baseline — benign-format harmful prompts under each defense level (measures defense refusal floor); (ii) no-defense baseline — each attack at each strength with L0 (measures raw ASR); (iii) single-technique baselines — every trick alone at each attacker strength and each defense level, so combined-technique effects decompose into main effects + interactions rather than being confounded with stacking.
2. Matched compute/query budgets: total target-model queries equalized across attacker-strength levels within each attack style (e.g., AutoDAN strong-with-fewer-restarts vs. weak-with-more-restarts variants checked for budget parity). Report queries-per-success alongside raw ASR.
3. Seeds and reproducibility: fixed seeds for GA initialization/mutation (AutoDAN), PAIR attacker sampling, paraphrasing, and smoothing perturbations; 2 independent seeds per cell minimum (more if budget allows — see feasibility) with seed as a random effect.
4. Trick-order permutation: within multi-trick combinations, at least 2 orderings sampled per cell to rule out ordering artifacts.
5. Benign-prompt over-refusal control: a fixed benign prompt set evaluated under every defense level to quantify over-refusal inflation, ensuring stronger defenses' apparent robustness is not trivially "refuse everything."
6. Judge robustness: two judges (primary + HarmBench classifier), a priori threshold, 0.3/0.7 sensitivity bands, ~10% human verification, and reporting of κ.
7. Identical materials across cells: same behavior sets, same judge, same defense implementations across both attack styles.

=====================================================================
(d) ANALYSIS PLAN
=====================================================================
Primary model: mixed-effects logistic regression on trial-level outcomes (behavior × cell):
  logit P(success) = β0 + βA·Attacker + βD·Defense + βT·TrickSet + βAD·(A×D) + βAT·(A×T) + βDT·(D×T) + βADT·(A×D×T) + stratification adjustments (dataset, attack style as stratum-specific intercepts and, in a pooled model, interactions with style) + random intercepts for behavior, model, and seed.
- Attacker/Defense entered as ordered categorical (or continuous level index in a sensitivity fit) to test monotone trends and their interaction shape.
- Interaction contrasts of interest: (i) A×D — is the defense-induced log-odds reduction smaller at high attacker strength (attenuation / arms-race)? (ii) A×D×T — do combined tricks specifically erode strong defenses? (iii) Style × A×D — does the interaction differ between token-level and prompt-level attacks? (iv) Dataset × A×D — generalization across benchmarks.
- Reporting: odds ratios with 95% CIs for interaction terms; marginal means (estimated marginal probabilities) per cell; simple-slopes plots of ASR vs. attacker strength by defense level; multiplicity controlled via Holm correction on the pre-registered interaction contrast family.
- Stratified analyses: models fit separately within each dataset and attack style stratum, plus pooled models with strata interactions; convergence between the two views is reported.
- Sensitivity analyses: judge threshold 0.3/0.7; secondary-judge refit; drop behaviors flagged ambiguous; per-model stratified refits to check that interactions are not driven by one model.

=====================================================================
(e) FEASIBILITY DISCUSSION — COMPUTE ESTIMATES AND RUNTIME ASSUMPTIONS
=====================================================================
Cell count (reference configuration): 2 attack styles × 3 attacker × 3 defense × 17 trick-sets × 3 models = 918 attack cells; × behaviors per cell × 2 seeds. With B behaviors per cell:
- Query cost per cell is attack-dependent: PAIR ≈ N×K attacker turns, each costing 1 target query + 1 attacker query (attacker model cost dominates; a 7–8B attacker keeps this cheap). AutoDAN cost ≈ pop × generations × queries-per-candidate evaluation + defense-induced multi-query overhead (SmoothLLM multiplies target queries by its perturbation count, e.g., ~10×) — this is the dominant budget driver and is why defense strength is capped at one strong arm.
- Reference budget: B = 50 behaviors per cell, 2 seeds → ~918 × 50 × 2 ≈ 92k attack trials; rough target-model query volume ~O(10^6–10^7) depending on defense overhead. On a single A100-class node with vLLM batched 7–8B inference, this is on the order of days, not weeks; AutoDAN cells dominate.
- Minimal-budget variant (fallback): B = 20 behaviors, 1 seed, trick factor reduced to {no-trick, best-2 singles, one 2-trick, one 3-trick} = 5 levels → 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 3 = 270 cells × 20 = 5.4k trials — a ~17× reduction that preserves the three-way structure with reduced trick-set resolution and wider CIs.
- Parameterization: everything scales linearly in (cells × B × seeds); the design is specified as (B, seeds, |trick levels|) knobs so the researcher can set the budget once known.
- Feasibility notes/risks: (i) if no GPU access materializes, the design cannot be executed as specified — it would need a cloud budget or a further 10× subsampling; (ii) SmoothLLM's query multiplier may force dropping it to a single defense level; (iii) AutoDAN's LLM-based token rewriting adds attacker-model cost comparable to PAIR; (iv) dataset availability (AdvBench, HarmBench) is public and assumed retrievable; (v) all numeric hyperparameters above are design assumptions with fallbacks, to be reconciled with setup_17/setup_18 details if the researcher later supplies them.

DELIVERABLE STATUS: complete design document only. No experiment was run, no code executed beyond workspace inspection, and no results are claimed.

Here's what I found and my proposed approach.

## (1) Inspection findings — present vs. absent

**Present:**
- `/workspace/task.json` only — containing the research question, the design-only context note, and a `track.md` document saying: *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."*
- Researcher topics provided: `neurips2024/97431/11:setup_17` and `setup_18` — suggesting the authoritative setup details (strength levels, tricks, defenses) are meant to come from a NeurIPS 2024 paper by topic, not from this workspace.

**Absent (confirmed by full directory scan):**
- No AutoDAN or PAIR attack code/implementations.
- No defense implementations (SmoothLLM, paraphrase filters, etc.).
- No datasets (AdvBench, HarmBench, etc.).
- No prior "tricks" logs, notes, configs, or seed files.
- No environment files or installed dependencies; network is disabled and GPU is not enabled — consistent with the design-only track.

So all concrete parameter values (attacker strength levels, defense list, trick inventory) must be sourced from the researcher's supplied setup topics rather than the repository.

## (2) Proposed high-level approach

**Design:** A crossed factorial experiment — Attacker Strength × Defense Strength × Trick Combination — run separately for AutoDAN (token-level) and PAIR (prompt-level), stratified by dataset.

**Independent variables:**
- *Attacker strength* (method-specific operationalizations held conceptually parallel): for AutoDAN — number of GA generations, population size, number of restarts, token mutation budget; for PAIR — number of attacker iterations (depth N), breadth K, attacker-model strength, temperature. Each mapped to 3 ordered levels (weak / medium / strong) with equalized query/compute budgets.
- *Defense strength:* e.g., none → weak (light paraphrase/self-reminding) → strong (SmoothLLM-style randomized smoothing, output filtering, or robustly safety-tuned targets), also 3 levels.

=====================================================================
The research question asks how COMBINED jailbreak techniques — attacker strength, defense strength, and previously tested tricks — affect ASR, and what the interaction dynamics between attacker power and defense robustness look like across datasets and attack styles. This demands a design in which these factors are varied ORTHOGONALLY rather than one at a time, because the primary scientific objects are interaction effects, not main effects. A crossed factorial (Attacker Strength × Defense Strength × Trick Combination) run separately under AutoDAN (token-level) and PAIR (prompt-level), stratified by dataset, directly yields: (i) whether stronger attacks overcome stronger defenses (attacker × defense interaction — e.g., an "arms-race" crossover where defense gains shrink as attacker strength grows); (ii) whether tricks and attacker strength substitute or complement (trick × attacker interaction); and (iii) whether these patterns generalize across datasets and across token-level vs. prompt-level attack styles (stratification). Prior-tested tricks enter as an explicit experimental factor rather than a fixed recipe, so their incremental and combined contribution is estimated rather than assumed. - PAIR operationalization (prompt-level): Weak = depth N=3, breadth K=1, smaller attacker model; Medium = N=10, K=4; Strong = N=20, K=6, strongest available attacker model, temperature raised modestly for exploration.
- Cross-method comparability: "strength" is WITHIN-STYLE only; no numeric cross-style equivalence is claimed. Instead, both styles are matched on total target-model query budget per cell (see Controls), so strength is not confounded with raw search effort.

FACTOR 2 — DEFENSE STRENGTH (3-tier ladder; design assumption).
- L0 None (raw model) — baseline.
- L1 Weak: light input-side defenses — paraphrase-based input smoothing or system-prompt self-reminding.
- L2 Strong: robust defenses — SmoothLLM-style randomized smoothing with perturbation+vote, and/or output filtering; if infeasible, substitute a safety-hardened target variant as the "strong defense" arm (fallback noted).

FACTOR 5 (stratification) — DATASET: AdvBench (stratified subsample of the 520 behaviors) + a second benchmark subset (e.g., HarmBench), giving two dataset strata.
